source.trial: Flather ACE-inhibitor individual-patient overview
source.citation: Flather MD et al. ACE-Inhibitor Myocardial Infarction Collaborative Group. Lancet 2000;355:1575-81

population: Five long-term ACEi-vs-placebo trials (SAVE, AIRE, TRACE, SOLVD-T, SOLVD-P), LV dysfunction or HF, 3 of 5 post-MI; 12,763 patients
quote: For all five trials the ACE inhibitor group had lower rates of death than the placebo group (1,467/6,391 [23.0%] vs 1,710/6,372 [26.8%]; 0.80 [0.74-0.87]) and lower rates of reinfarction (571 [8.9%] vs 703 [11.0%]; 0.79 [0.70-0.89]), readmission for heart failure (876 [13.7%] vs 1202 [18.9%]; 0.67 [0.61-0.74]), and the composite of these events (2161 [33.8%] vs 2610 [41.0%]; 0.72 [0.67-0.78]; all p<0.0001).
notes: Peto odds ratio (not a hazard ratio), all-cause death, average follow-up 35 months. Shared by lisinopril, enalapril, ramipril and captopril per the class rule (no placebo-controlled lisinopril trial exists). Three of five trials were post-infarction; only SOLVD-T/P enrolled chronic HF.

source.trial: CHARM-Overall (candesartan vs placebo, all EF)
source.citation: Pfeffer MA et al. Lancet 2003;362:759-66

population: CHARM programme, LVEF <=40 and >40, candesartan vs placebo
quote: 886 (23%) patients in the candesartan and 945 (25%) in the placebo group died (unadjusted hazard ratio 0.91 [95% CI 0.83-1.00], p=0.055; covariate adjusted 0.90 [0.82-0.99], p=0.032)
extrapolation: No ACE-inhibitor placebo trial enrolled LVEF 41-49%. A band-specific all-cause death HR for LVEF 40-49 (Lund 2018, Eur J Heart Fail 29431256) is in the full text, which was not retrievable (paywalled, not in PMC); the Lund abstract and the secondary sources found give no all-cause figure for this band. Used the programme-wide HR, whose abstract states 'Ejection fraction or treatment at baseline did not alter these effects'. ACEi value is carried over from the ARB (CHARM) estimate as the nearest evidence.
notes: Unadjusted HR; covariate-adjusted 0.90 (0.82-0.99). Weak for this band: all-EF average, not LVEF 40-49. Young 2004 (EF<=40) all-cause HR 0.88 (0.79-0.98); Cochrane 2021 ARB at EF>40 RR 1.01 (0.92-1.11), so the true band value lies between.

source.trial: CHARM pooled by EF (Lund 2018), time-to-first HF hospitalization, quoted via ESC Heart Fail 2023 network meta-analysis
source.citation: Lund LH et al. Eur J Heart Fail 2018;20:1230-9 (29431256); quoted in Leite M et al. ESC Heart Fail 2023;10:1822-34

population: CHARM, HFmrEF (EF 40-49%), n=1322, candesartan vs placebo
quote: Candesartan significantly reduced the composite endpoint of CV death or HF hospitalization (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.61-0.96; P = 0.02), first HF hospitalization (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.55-0.95; P = 0.02), and HF hospitalization recurrence (HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.33-0.70; P < 0.001) in HFmrEF subgroup.
extrapolation: No ACEi placebo trial in LVEF 41-49%; the ARB (candesartan, CHARM) estimate is applied as the nearest evidence. Time-to-first HF hospitalization HR chosen over the recurrent-event rate ratio 0.48 (0.33-0.70) per the rule.
notes: Post hoc EF split of a trial; 1322 patients. Lund 2018 abstract itself gives only the recurrent-event rate ratio (0.48 (0.33-0.70)) and the first-event composite HR 0.76 (0.61-0.96); the first-HFH HR 0.72 comes from the 2023 network meta-analysis text, not the Lund full text.

source.trial: CHARM low-LVEF pool (CHARM-Alternative + CHARM-Added)
source.citation: Young JB et al. Circulation 2004;110:2618-26 (CHARM low-LVEF trials)

population: CHARM-Alternative + CHARM-Added, LVEF <=40, n=4576 (2289 candesartan, 2287 placebo); CHARM-Alternative = ACE-inhibitor-intolerant, CHARM-Added = on ACE inhibitor
quote: Of the patients in the candesartan group, 817 (35.7%) experienced cardiovascular death or a CHF hospitalization as compared with 944 (41.3%) in the placebo group (HR 0.82; 95% CI 0.74 to 0.90; P<0.001) with reduced risk for both cardiovascular deaths (521 [22.8%] versus 599 [26.2%]; HR 0.84 [95% CI 0.75 to 0.95]; P=0.005) and CHF hospitalizations (516 [22.5%] versus 642 [28.1%]; HR 0.76 [95% CI 0.68 to 0.85]; P<0.001). It is important to note that all-cause mortality also was significantly reduced by candesartan (642 [28.0%] versus 708 [31.0%]; HR 0.88 [95% CI 0.79 to 0.98]; P=0.018).
extrapolation: CHARM-Alternative alone (ACEi-intolerant) is the preferred class evidence, but its abstract (Granger 2003, PMID 13678870) gives only the composite HR 0.77 (0.67-0.89) and 'each component ... was reduced'; the component HRs are in the paywalled full text. Fell back to the prespecified CHARM low-LVEF pool (Young 2004), as the rule allows. Cross-check: dividing the McMurray 2015 putative-placebo all-cause figure referenced to CHARM-Alternative (0.74 (0.61-0.89)) by PARADIGM-HF vs enalapril (0.84 (0.76-0.93)) on the log scale gives about 0.88 (0.75-1.03) for CHARM-Alternative, in line with 0.88.
notes: Time-to-first-event analysis, all-cause death, a secondary endpoint in the pooled analysis. Val-HeFT (valsartan, ~93% on an ACE inhibitor; 'Overall mortality was similar in the two groups', abstract gives no ratio) recorded but not used. Shared by valsartan, candesartan, losartan (no placebo-controlled losartan trial).

source.trial: Cochrane review, ACE inhibitors vs placebo/no treatment, LVEF >40%
source.citation: Martin N et al. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2021;5:CD012721

population: 5 RCTs, 1187 patients, LVEF >40% (3 placebo-controlled, others usual-care comparator); includes PEP-CHF, Hong Kong DHF, Zi 2003
quote: Pooled analyses with moderate-certainty evidence suggest that ACEI treatment likely has little or no effect on cardiovascular mortality (RR 0.93, 95% CI 0.61 to 1.42; 945 participants; two studies), all-cause mortality (RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.75 to 1.45; 1187 participants; five studies) and heart failure hospitalisation (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.64 to 1.15; 1019 participants; three studies)
notes: Risk ratio on patients dying; PEP-CHF alone HR 1.09 (0.75-1.58). Population is LVEF >40, not >=50. Replaces the earlier assumed-neutral 1.0 with a published randomized estimate; it is neutral-leaning and imprecise.

population: 2 RCTs, 7148 patients, LVEF >40%

source.trial: PARADIGM-HF putative-placebo analysis (reference: SOLVD-T enalapril vs placebo)
source.citation: McMurray J et al. Eur Heart J 2015;36:434-9

population: PARADIGM-HF (LVEF <=40) vs enalapril, indirectly referenced to placebo
quote: For the primary composite outcome of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization in PARADIGM-HF, the relative risk reduction with LCZ696 vs. a putative placebo from SOLVD-T was 43% (95%CI 34-50%; P < 0.0001) with similarly large effects on cardiovascular death (34%, 21-44%; P < 0.0001) and heart failure hospitalization (49%, 39-58%; P < 0.0001). For all-cause mortality, the reduction compared with a putative placebo was 28% (95%CI 15-39%; P < 0.0001).
extrapolation: Published indirect comparison: product of LCZ696-vs-enalapril HR (death 0.84 (0.76-0.93), PMID 25176015) and SOLVD-T enalapril-vs-placebo; converted from a 28% reduction (15-39%) to 0.72 (0.61-0.85).
notes: Not a randomized placebo comparison. Referenced to CHARM-Alternative instead: 26% (11-39%) = 0.74 (0.61-0.89). It uses SOLVD-T, whereas the ACEi class row uses the Flather overview (0.80), so ARNI-vs-ACEi in the engine is 0.72 vs 0.80, slightly larger than the randomized 0.84.

source.trial: PARADIGM-HF putative-placebo analysis (reference: SOLVD-T enalapril vs placebo)
source.citation: McMurray J et al. Eur Heart J 2015;36:434-9

population: PARADIGM-HF (LVEF <=40) vs enalapril, indirectly referenced to placebo
quote: For the primary composite outcome of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization in PARADIGM-HF, the relative risk reduction with LCZ696 vs. a putative placebo from SOLVD-T was 43% (95%CI 34-50%; P < 0.0001) with similarly large effects on cardiovascular death (34%, 21-44%; P < 0.0001) and heart failure hospitalization (49%, 39-58%; P < 0.0001). For all-cause mortality, the reduction compared with a putative placebo was 28% (95%CI 15-39%; P < 0.0001).
extrapolation: Converted from a 49% reduction (39-58%) to 0.51 (0.42-0.61). Time-to-first HF hospitalization.
notes: Indirect. CHARM-Alternative-referenced: 46% (33-56%) = 0.54 (0.44-0.67).

source.trial: Solomon 2020 pooled PARADIGM-HF + PARAGON-HF (ARNI vs RAS inhibitor) x CHARM-Overall (RAS blocker vs placebo)
source.citation: Solomon SD et al. Circulation 2020;141:352-61; Pfeffer MA et al. Lancet 2003;362:759-66

population: PARADIGM+PARAGON pooled, all EF (n=13,195) vs ACEi/ARB; times candesartan vs placebo (all EF)
quote: Overall sacubitril/valsartan was superior to renin-angiotensin-aldosterone-system inhibition for first cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization (Hazard Ratio [HR] 0.84 [95% CI, 0.78-0.90]), cardiovascular death (HR 0.84 [95% CI, 0.76-0.92]), heart failure hospitalization (HR 0.84 [95% CI, 0.77-0.91]), and all-cause mortality (HR 0.88 [95% CI, 0.81-0.96]).
extrapolation: Log-scale product. (a) ARNI vs RAS inhibitor, all-cause death 0.88 (0.81-0.96): ln=-0.1278, se=(ln0.96-ln0.81)/3.92=0.0433. (b) ACEi/ARB vs placebo, mildly reduced band, all-cause death 0.91 (0.83-1.00) (CHARM-Overall, row ARB-mildly_reduced-death): ln=-0.0943, se=(ln1.00-ln0.83)/3.92=0.0475. Sum ln=-0.2221, combined se=sqrt(0.0433^2+0.0475^2)=0.0643; rr=exp(-0.2221)=0.80, interval exp(-0.2221 +/- 1.96*0.0643)=0.71-0.91.
notes: Arithmetic matches the first researcher. Both components are all-EF averages (band-specific HRs for Solomon 2020 are in figures not retrievable; the abstract says benefit is 'primarily below the normal range' and effect varies by LVEF, interaction P=0.02). Independence assumed. Weakest ARNI death cell.

source.trial: Solomon 2020 pooled PARADIGM-HF + PARAGON-HF (ARNI vs RAS inhibitor) x CHARM HFmrEF first-HFH (RAS blocker vs placebo)
source.citation: Solomon SD et al. Circulation 2020;141:352-61; Lund LH et al. Eur J Heart Fail 2018 as quoted in Leite M et al. ESC Heart Fail 2023

population: PARADIGM+PARAGON pooled, all EF, first HF hospitalization vs ACEi/ARB; times candesartan HFmrEF first-HFH vs placebo
quote: Overall sacubitril/valsartan was superior to renin-angiotensin-aldosterone-system inhibition for first cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization (Hazard Ratio [HR] 0.84 [95% CI, 0.78-0.90]), cardiovascular death (HR 0.84 [95% CI, 0.76-0.92]), heart failure hospitalization (HR 0.84 [95% CI, 0.77-0.91]), and all-cause mortality (HR 0.88 [95% CI, 0.81-0.96]).
extrapolation: Log-scale product. (a) ARNI vs RAS inhibitor, first HF hospitalization 0.84 (0.77-0.91): ln=-0.1744, se=(ln0.91-ln0.77)/3.92=0.0426. (b) ACEi/ARB vs placebo, mildly reduced, time-to-first HF hospitalization 0.72 (0.55-0.95): ln=-0.3285, se=(ln0.95-ln0.55)/3.92=0.1394. Sum ln=-0.5029, se=sqrt(0.0426^2+0.1394^2)=0.1458; rr=exp(-0.5029)=0.605, interval exp(-0.5029 +/- 1.96*0.1458)=0.45-0.81.
notes: Corrects the first researcher's 0.40 (0.27-0.59), whose arithmetic was right but which multiplied in the recurrent-event rate ratio 0.48 instead of the first-event HR 0.72. Component (a) is an all-EF average dominated by PARADIGM-HF (HFrEF); the abstract says HFH benefit extends to mildly reduced EF. Still the weakest-grounded ARNI cell: two indirect factors, one from a post hoc subgroup.

source.trial: Cochrane 2021 ARNI vs usual care/valsartan (PARAGON-HF, PARAMOUNT, PARALLAX) x Cochrane 2021 ARB vs placebo (all-cause death)
source.citation: Martin N et al. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2021;5:CD012721

population: HFpEF/LVEF >40-45, ARNI vs valsartan or usual care (7663 patients); times ARB vs placebo (7964 patients)
quote: The three studies reported data for all-cause mortality (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.84 to 1.11; 7663 participants; three studies; high-certainty evidence; Analysis 5.5).
extrapolation: Log-scale product. (a) ARNI vs valsartan/usual care, all-cause death RR 0.97 (0.84-1.11): ln=-0.0305, se=(ln1.11-ln0.84)/3.92=0.0711. (b) ARB vs placebo, preserved band, all-cause death RR 1.01 (0.92-1.11) (row ARB-preserved-death): ln=0.0100, se=(ln1.11-ln0.92)/3.92=0.0479. Sum ln=-0.0206, se=sqrt(0.0711^2+0.0479^2)=0.0857; rr=exp(-0.0206)=0.98, interval exp(-0.0206 +/- 1.96*0.0857)=0.83-1.16.
notes: Replaces the first researcher's CV-death proxy 0.95 (0.79-1.16) with all-cause death. PARALLAX's comparator was individualized medical therapy, not purely an ARB. Pooled PARADIGM+PARAGON all-EF death 0.88 (0.81-0.96) not used here because it is dominated by HFrEF.

source.trial: Cochrane 2021 ARNI vs usual care/valsartan (PARAGON-HF + PARALLAX, first HFH) x Cochrane 2021 ARB vs placebo (first HFH)
source.citation: Martin N et al. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2021;5:CD012721

population: ARNI vs valsartan/usual care, 7362 patients, EF >40-45; times ARB vs placebo, 7148 patients
quote: PARAGON-HF and PARALLAX also reported HRs for time to first hospitalisation due to HF, which gives a pooled effect of HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.76 to 0.99; 7362 participants; two studies; I² = 82%; Analysis 5.3).
extrapolation: Log-scale product. (a) ARNI vs valsartan/usual care, time to first HF hospitalization HR 0.87 (0.76-0.99): ln=-0.1393, se=(ln0.99-ln0.76)/3.92=0.0674. (b) ARB vs placebo, preserved, time-to-first HR 0.90 (0.80-1.01) (row ARB-preserved-hfh): ln=-0.1054, se=(ln1.01-ln0.80)/3.92=0.0595. Sum ln=-0.2447, se=sqrt(0.0674^2+0.0595^2)=0.0899; rr=exp(-0.2447)=0.78, interval exp(-0.2447 +/- 1.96*0.0899)=0.66-0.93.
notes: Replaces 0.66 (0.48-0.92), which multiplied two recurrent-event rate ratios (PARAGON total HFH 0.85 x CHARM 0.78). Heterogeneity between the two ARNI trials is large (I2=82%). Vaduganathan 2023 (PARAGLIDE-HF + PARAGON-HF, PMID 37210743) reports only the composite of total worsening-HF events and CV death (all participants RR 0.86 (0.75-0.98)), no separate HFH or death figure, so it is not usable for these cells.

source.trial: Fixed-effect pool of CIBIS-II (bisoprolol), MERIT-HF (metoprolol CR/XL), COPERNICUS (carvedilol)
source.citation: CIBIS-II Lancet 1999;353:9-13; MERIT-HF Lancet 1999;353:2001-7; COPERNICUS N Engl J Med 2001;344:1651-8

population: LVEF <=35 (CIBIS-II), <=40 (MERIT-HF), <25 (COPERNICUS); NYHA II-IV, on ACEi/diuretic
quote: CIBIS-II: All-cause mortality was significantly lower with bisoprolol than on placebo (156 [11.8%] vs 228 [17.3%] deaths with a hazard ratio of 0.66 (95% CI 0.54-0.81, p<0.0001). MERIT-HF: ... relative risk 0.66 [95% CI 0.53-0.81] ... COPERNICUS: ... a 35 percent decrease in the risk of death with carvedilol (95 percent confidence interval, 19 to 48 percent ...).
extrapolation: Inverse-variance fixed-effect pool on the log scale. Inputs: CIBIS-II 0.66 (0.54-0.81), se=0.1034; MERIT-HF 0.66 (0.53-0.81), se=0.1082; COPERNICUS 0.65 (0.52-0.81; from a 35% decrease, 19-48%), se=0.1131. Weights 1/se^2: 93.5, 85.4, 78.2; pooled ln = -0.4202, se=0.0624; rr=0.657, interval 0.58-0.74.
notes: No published class pool at LVEF <40 quotable as a single number: Cleland 2018 (29040525) reports sinus-rhythm strata only; pooling its four strata <40 (<20, 20-25, 26-34, 35-39, adjusted HRs) gives 0.73 (0.67-0.80), weaker because that IPD set also contains bucindolol (BEST), nebivolol (SENIORS) and others. Shibata 2001 (Eur J Heart Fail, 11378007): 22 trials, death OR 0.63 (0.55-0.72) (Peto OR). The three formulary drugs are the three pooled trials, so their pool is used. Same estimate for carvedilol, metoprolol succinate and bisoprolol (class rule).

source.trial: CIBIS-II (bisoprolol), applied to the class
source.citation: CIBIS-II Investigators. Lancet 1999;353:9-13

population: LVEF <=35, NYHA III-IV, on ACEi/diuretic
quote: Hospitalizations for worsening heart failure were also decreased by 32% (18% placebo v 12% bisoprolol, hazard ratio .64; 95% CI, .53 to .79; P< .0001).
extrapolation: MERIT-HF and COPERNICUS HF-hospitalization-alone ratios with intervals could not be retrieved (MERIT-HF abstract: total mortality or HF hospitalization 311 vs 439 events, risk reduction 31% (20-40%), HF hospitalizations 317 vs 451 events; COPERNICUS abstract: death or HF hospitalization reduced 31%, P=0.000004, no interval), so no pool was possible.
notes: NOT directly verified: the quote is from a protocol document surfaced by search that cites CIBIS-II; the CIBIS-II Lancet abstract has no hospitalization figure and the full text is paywalled. Corroboration from verified sources: Shibata 2001 (11378007) class OR for HF admissions 0.63 (11.3% vs 17.1%; CI not in abstract); MERIT-HF crude event ratio 317/451 = 0.70. Time-to-first HR. Same value for carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol.

source.trial: Beta-blockers in Heart Failure Collaborative Group IPD meta-analysis (Cleland 2018), sinus rhythm, LVEF 40-49%
source.citation: Cleland JGF et al. Eur Heart J 2018;39:26-35

population: Sinus rhythm, LVEF 40-49%, n=575, 11 double-blind placebo-controlled trials

source.citation: Cleland JGF et al. Eur Heart J 2018;39:26-35 (Table 2, open-access full text)

population: Sinus rhythm, LVEF 40-49%, n=566 (CV hospitalization)

extrapolation: Reduced band: pool of the four sinus-rhythm strata below 40% for cardiovascular hospitalization (<20: 0.70 (0.60-0.81); 20-25: 0.75 (0.66-0.85); 26-34: 0.84 (0.74-0.94); 35-39: 0.75 (0.61-0.91)), inverse-variance on the log scale = 0.768 (0.716-0.824). source.trial: Cleland 2018 IPD (LVEF >=50, sinus rhythm) vs Zheng 2018 and Cochrane 2021 (LVEF >40/>=40) meta-analyses
source.citation: Cleland JGF et al. Eur Heart J 2018;39:26-35; Zheng SL et al. Heart 2018;104:407-15; Martin N et al. Cochrane 2021;CD012721

population: Sinus rhythm LVEF >=50 (n=241 analysed) and trials with LVEF >=40/>40 (SENIORS subgroup EF >35%, J-DHF, small RCTs)

source.trial: SELECT HFrEF subgroup (semaglutide) pooled with FIGHT + LIVE (liraglutide)
source.citation: Deanfield J, et al. Lancet 2024;404:773-86; Margulies KB, et al. JAMA 2016 (FIGHT); Christophides, J Clin Med 2026 (FIGHT + LIVE pooled)

population: Semaglutide 2.4 mg in SELECT patients with prevalent HF: 4286 (1347 investigator-defined HFrEF, 2273 HFpEF, 666 unclassified); ASCVD with BMI >=27, mostly not recently hospitalized; median follow-up ~3 years

source.trial: Cochrane review of diuretics for chronic HF
source.citation: Faris RF, et al. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2012;(2):CD003838

population: Chronic HF with fluid retention (congestion); Cochrane 2012 placebo-controlled trials, EF bands not separated
quote: Mortality was lower for participants treated with diuretics than for placebo, odds ratio (OR) for death 0.24, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.07 to 0.83; P = 0.02. Admission for worsening heart failure was reduced in those taking diuretics in two trials (169 participants), OR 0.07 (95% CI 0.01 to 0.52; P = 0.01).
extrapolation: Owner ruling 2026-11-16: "use the Cochrane diuretic figures for congested patients". Applies when the patient has congestion by the engine's congestion predicate. The trials did not report by EF band; the figure is used for the reduced band as the nearest match (most participants had reduced EF).
notes: EVIDENCE FOR benefit: Cochrane 2012 (14 trials, 525 participants, 7 placebo-controlled): mortality in 3 placebo-controlled trials (202 participants) OR 0.24 (95% CI 0.07-0.83; P=0.02); admission for worsening HF in 2 trials (169 participants) OR 0.07 (0.01-0.52; P=0.01). AGAINST using those numbers: tiny pre-ACE-inhibitor/beta-blocker/MRA/SGLT2i trials, implausibly large effects, and a no-diuretic arm cannot be rerun in congested patients. NO DIFFERENCE between loops: TRANSFORM-HF (torsemide vs furosemide, n=2859): death 373/1431 (26.1%) vs 374/1428 (26.2%), HR 1.02 (0.89-1.18); total hospitalizations rate ratio 0.94 (0.84-1.07); 'Results were similar across prespecified subgroups, including among patients with reduced, mildly reduced, or preserved ejection fraction' (JAMA 2023, PMID 36648467). DOSE (PMID 21366472) compared bolus vs infusion and low vs high dose, not drug vs none. Furoscix/SC furosemide: no outcome trial vs none; SUBCUT-HF II (PMID 42872757) tested an early-discharge strategy (HF readmissions 13 [14%] vs 5 [6%], OR 2.45, 0.81-7.43), not the drug. OWNER RULING 2026-11-16: "use the Cochrane diuretic figures for congested patients" (the alternative offered was neutral, 1.0). The controller had already entered these figures earlier the same day on its own reading of the owner's evidence rule (best estimates carried with their uncertainty, no all-or-nothing cut-offs). Three (death) and two (admission for worsening HF) small placebo-controlled trials from the 1980s-90s, before modern therapy (before ACE inhibitors, beta-blockers, MRAs and SGLT2 inhibitors became standard); the trials enrolled patients with fluid retention; EF bands were not separated, so the same figure is used in each band (reduced band: meta_analysis; mildly reduced and preserved rows: extrapolated). The interval is wide because the trials are small; it is carried into the score, not replaced by zero. Odds ratios are used as relative risks (an approximation that overstates the effect when events are common).

source.trial: CLOROTIC (HCTZ added to IV furosemide)
source.citation: Trullas JC, et al. Eur Heart J 2023;44:411-21; EF split JACC Heart Fail 2024;12:1719-30 (PMID 38934966)

population: Acute HF inpatients (median LVEF 55%), n=230; no chronic outcome trial
quote: There were no differences in mortality or rehospitalizations.
extrapolation: No direct randomized evidence of benefit or harm for this outcome in this band; assumed neutral (rr 1.0, null interval) per controller ruling 2026-11-15 (not ruled by the owner).
notes: EVIDENCE: CLOROTIC (230 acute-HF inpatients, median LVEF 55%, 72% LVEF >40%; HCTZ vs placebo added to IV furosemide for 4 days): 'There were no differences in mortality or rehospitalizations'; the EF-split paper: 'no significant differences observed with the addition of HCTZ in terms of mortality, rehospitalizations, or safety endpoints ... among the 2 LVEF groups'. OWNER DECISION: neutral (1.0).

quote: CONCLUSION: Concurrent use of patiromer and high-dose MRAs reduces the risk of recurrent hyperkalemia (DIAMOND). Composite of cardiovascular (CV) death or worsening HF occurred in 11 (11%) participants in the SZC group ... and 3 (3%) participants in the placebo group (REALIZE-K).
extrapolation: No direct randomized evidence of benefit or harm for this outcome in this band; assumed neutral (rr 1.0, null interval) per controller ruling 2026-11-15 (not ruled by the owner).
notes: EVIDENCE: DIAMOND (patiromer, HFrEF with RAASi-related hyperkalemia, 439 vs 439 randomized, median 27 weeks): its primary endpoint was REVISED from time to CV death/CV hospitalization to change in potassium (full text: 'the primary endpoint was revised during the study from time to first occurrence of cardiovascular death or cardiovascular hospitalization, to changes in serum potassium levels'); no clinical-event HR was reported. Effects were on potassium (HR 0.63 for K >5.5) and MRA dose reduction (HR 0.62), so any benefit is indirect, via enabling RAAS inhibitor/MRA. AGAINST (SZC): REALIZE-K (n=203, LVEF <=40%): 'Composite of cardiovascular (CV) death or worsening HF occurred in 11 (11%) participants in the SZC group (1 with CV death, 10 with HF events) and 3 (3%) participants in the placebo group (1 with CV death, 2 with HF events; log-rank nominal P = 0.034)'; an exploratory endpoint on 12 events, so not entered as an estimate but a safety signal for SZC. OWNER DECISION: neutral (1.0) for both; the engine should credit binders only through MRA/RAASi enablement.
